text:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT 4921 — elevated p95/p99 latency on inference-serving (hosted API). Auto-alert trigged at 02:12 UTC: backend queue depth increasing, GPU pods hitting sustained stall. Paging oncall.
oncall-bot: paging emily (SRE oncall)
emily: I’m on it. looking at metrics now. p95 jumped from 120ms -> 980ms over last 6m, p99 ~2.8s. CPU on runtime nodes spiked, backlog of reqs in the router.
dave: runtime here — saw large number of streaming connections holding KV cache active. baseline batching under pressure. suspect streaming keep-alive + long-lived chats are preventing efficient batching.
hana: confirming — streaming token throughput dropped per-GPU efficiency by ~30%. Non-streaming requests still fine but overall queueing causing latency to climb and client timeouts.
emily: what's the customer impact? pj: product — a few enterprise customers seeing partial failures on chat sessions. Support triage reporting increased 504s for streaming endpoints. No billing impact alert yet but some customers reported UX regressions.
carla: elevator: can we do a knob to reduce streaming concurrency or fall back to poll/non-streaming for new sessions? We shouldn't break existing sessions if possible.
dave: we have two quick mitigations: 1) global throttle on new streaming sessions via edge policy (reject or return 429 for new streaming create). 2) flip feature flag to disable streaming responses temporarily, forcing clients to the non-streaming path. 1 is safer but slower to reduce pressure; 2 is blunt but effective.
emily: prefer 1 first. can we rate-limit new streaming sessions to 20r/s across region and enforce per-customer quota? if that doesn't knock down queueing in 5m, we can escalate to full disable.
dave: edge policy ready: /policies/streaming-create rate-limit=20/s region=us-west-1,us-east-1. applying now. patch shown to ops log:
```
PATCH /edge/policies/streaming-create
{"limit":20, "burst":40, "scope":"global"}
```
emily: applied. watching.
(3m later)
emily: p95 down to 430ms, p99 1.5s, queue depth still above normal but trending down. new streaming creates dropped ~65%.
pj: support update sent to affected customers — advising degraded streaming, recommending re-try or switch to poll endpoint.
hana: backend GPU stalls still happening intermittently. older sessions still keep KV caches pinned; long-lived sessions remain hot.
carla: can we target long-lived sessions for graceful drain? maybe TTL existing streaming sessions to terminate after X minutes so they fall back to non-streaming on reconnect.
dave: we can issue a controlled disconnect for sessions older than 10m. code snippet (internal admin tool):
```
POST /admin/sessions/terminate
{"filter": "type:streaming AND age>600", "grace_seconds": 10}
```
emily: that will impact some active users. want to avoid user-visible abrupt drops unless necessary. timeline: if throttling + session drain doesn't stabilize in 10m, prepare for full streaming disable.
dave: preflight for full disable: a feature-flag flip at control plane. command:
```
# internal only
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/flags/streaming -d '{"state":"off","reason":"mitigation: INC-4921"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>"
```
hana: what happens client-side? SDKs will fall back to non-streaming endpoints; some integrations may see slightly higher latency per request but much more predictable token throughput.
carla: ops: prepare rollback script. also prepare a config to route 20% of traffic to streaming canary when we re-enable.
emily: agree. also open a JIRA and tag oncall handoff.
incidents-bot: created INC-4921 in tracker (link: https://incidents/redwood/INC-4921)
emily: scheduled handoff to dave in 30m (my shift ends at 03:00 UTC). dave will be primary responder and hana will keep monitoring infra.
dave: taking over in 30. summary for next shift: throttled new streaming creates to 20/s global at 02:16 UTC; observed latency improvement but long-lived sessions still holding hot KV caches. plan if regress: 1) graceful terminate sessions age>10m 2) flip streaming flag off 3) update customer comms and reopen support ticket batch.
emily: 10m check — still trending. if we hit p95>700ms again, execute session terminate.
(10m later)
emily: p95 back up to 760ms. initiating session terminate for streaming sessions >10m, grace 12s. issuing now.
incidents-bot: admin request submitted, job id job-98123
dave: saw ~18% of sessions drop, reconnects landed on non-streaming path. immediate queue depth relief. p95 down to 340ms, p99 900ms.
pj: support updated customers with next steps and ETA for full restore.
emily: given improvement but still some instability on tail. recommending we flip streaming off for new/old sessions until kernel-level patch next deploy. (vote: emily yes, dave yes, hana yes, pj neutral)
dave: executing feature-flag flip to OFF. posting cmd in ops log and then executing:
```
# flip streaming OFF
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/flags/streaming -d '{"state":"off","reason":"INC-4921 - temporary mitigation"}'
```
incidents-bot: feature flag streaming=OFF applied at 02:45 UTC. router returning header: X-Streaming-Enabled: false
emily: monitor. note: we'll have degraded UX for streaming clients but service availability prioritized.
(5m later)
emily: metrics: p95 210ms, p99 430ms, queue depth normal. error rate on non-streaming path increased slightly but within SLA. number of affected streaming sessions: ~4200 reconnections to poll path.
pj: sending customer status update noting mitigation and expected next steps.
carla: tracking follow-ups: (1) postmortem, (2) patch to runtime to improve streaming KV eviction, (3) improved per-customer streaming quotas and graceful session TTL, (4) canary plan to re-enable streaming safely.
emily: handing off to dave now. I'm signing out. dave — you own the mitigation, please keep incident page updated and coordinate with runtime team for the patch rollout.
dave: acknowledged. will keep monitoring through my shift and announce re-enable plan after kernel patch + controlled canary.
incidents-bot: incident INC-4921 status: mitigated -> controlled mitigation (streaming disabled) at 02:45 UTC. ongoing monitoring. assigned to dave. link: https://incidents/redwood/INC-4921
emily: thanks team :heart:
carla: good job. please prepare short customer-facing RCA once we have root cause.
dave: will do — initial suspected root cause: long-lived streaming sessions preventing efficient batching + KV cache pressure causing GPU stalls; runtime patch and eviction improvements targeted. more detail after logs and heap profiles.
